points.text: `NamesOnlyTests.test_prints_only_names` asserts the exact order `Cafe du Pont` (300 m) then `Cafe Lumiere` (120 m). That is today's farthest-first order, and the `names-only` entry says nothing about order. The test therefore pins an incidental behavior, probably a bug, that the ticket did not ask to specify. Whoever fixes the sort will break this test for no reason related to `--names-only`. Fix: compare the lines in an order-independent way (for example sorted, or as a set), and keep asserting that there is no distance and no count line. Separately, farthest-first looks questionable against the overview's "sorts by distance". It is out of scope for #74, so I am not blocking on it. The author may open a `type:bug` ticket.

The PR body says "not by command: it is a trivial option", so the PR shows no check that the CLI really behaves as described. The unit test only covers the query `cafe`. Run `--names-only` through the CLI and record the real output in the PR body. Add a test for the second half of the entry ("Without the option the output is unchanged") if the existing tests do not already cover it. Also state or test what `--names-only` does with a query that matches nothing, since the entry says nothing about it. Prove that case, or leave it out of the claim.

The entry has two statements: with `--names-only` the output is one name per line with no distance and no count, and without it the output is unchanged. The PR tests only the first (`NamesOnlyTests.test_prints_only_names`). Add a test for the same query `cafe` without the option that asserts the existing output, including the distance and count lines. Without it the 'unchanged' promise is unchecked, and the entry is being moved to `implemented`.

The PR body says 'Verified: names-only — not by command: it is a trivial option'. I did not accept that. I re-ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests` on the branch (10 tests, OK), but that run does not cover the unchanged-output half of the entry. After adding the test, replace the line with the real command and its observed output, for example `python -m accessplaces.cli cafe --names-only` and the same query without the option. Also make sure the history shows the failing test commit before the implementation commit. I could not confirm that from what I was given.

The entry has two clauses: `--names-only` prints one name per line with no distance and no count, and without the option the output is unchanged. The PR moves it to `implemented`, but its only test, `NamesOnlyTests.test_prints_only_names`, covers the first clause. Nothing checks that the default output (distance and count line) is unchanged after the cli.py edit. Add a regression test that runs the same `cafe` query without the option and asserts the previous output exactly. The 10 tests I re-ran pass, but none of them is stated to cover this clause.

The PR body says "Verified: names-only — not by command: it is a trivial option". That justification does not hold. The behavior is a CLI output contract, and the unchanged-output clause was never exercised. Once the regression test is added, update the line to name the command actually run, for example `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and the CLI invocation with and without `--names-only`.

The new test fixes the line order as `Cafe du Pont` (300 m) then `Cafe Lumiere` (120 m). That is farthest first, which is how `search()` behaves today. The product is described as sorting by distance, and nearest first is the usual reading. Neither the `names-only` entry nor ticket #74 states an order, so the test locks in a behavior that may be a latent bug. I have no fix to propose until a human answers. Options: (a) farthest first is intended, so the order goes into the wiki; (b) it is a bug, so open a separate `type:bug` ticket and keep this test's order out of this PR, for example by comparing the set of lines or a sorted list. The PR cannot settle this alone.

The entry makes two promises: the option prints names only, and "without the option the output is unchanged". The PR adds only NamesOnlyTests.test_prints_only_names, which covers the first. Nothing in the diff shows a test pinning the default output (distance and count line) for the same query. Add one, or point to an existing test that already asserts it, so the move to `implemented` is backed for both promises.

The PR body says "Verified: names-only — not by command: it is a trivial option". That is not verification. Run the real CLI with and without `--names-only` on the `cafe` query, and record the commands and their output in the PR body. My re-run of `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (10 tests, OK) only exercises the unit test.

The new test asserts the order `Cafe du Pont` (300 m), then `Cafe Lumiere` (120 m). That is farthest first, the current behavior of `search()`, which is probably a bug for a tool described as sorting by distance. Neither the entry nor the ticket states an order, so the test now pins an order nobody specified. A human has to choose between two options. Option 1: keep the current order and have the test assert it deliberately. Option 2: open a separate `type:bug` ticket for the sort and make this test order-independent, so it does not break when that is fixed. I am not deciding this inside a `type:tech` ticket.
